title: Load an ASTM D638 dogbone into two spring-closed wedge grips, jogging the test stand crosshead onto it
instruction: Mount the dogbone test specimen in the tensile tester: clamped flat and straight in both wedge grips at the 115 mm test length, both tab ends clear of the slot ends, and both arms clear of the stand and its control panel.
context: Before every tensile test a plastics QC technician mounts the specimen. ASTM D638 Type I specimens are 165 mm long with 115 mm between the grips. Wedge grips are spring-closed: one hand holds the lever open while the other slides the tab in through the grip's open-sided slot; the second grip, on the stand's crosshead, is jogged onto the other tab with the stand's key while its lever is held open. A specimen gripped at an angle, off the jaw centre or pushed against a slot end tears early and the result is discarded. New against bar-on-two-supports tasks: holding a spring-closed grip open while threading a 3.2 mm tab into its 6.2 mm opening, then driving the second grip onto the tab and clamping both straight. Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers (O*NET 51-9061), core task: "Inspect, test, or measure materials, products, installations, or work for conformance to specifications" (602,000 employees on O*NET; BLS OEWS May 2023: 584,630).
setup: Station table top 0.7475 m; origin midway between the arm bases, x forward, y left, metres. Green ESD bench mat 420 x 600 x 3 mm at (0.27, 0). Horizontal motorized force test stand (grey base 130 x 460 x 40 mm) along y at (0.30, 0), loading axis 76 mm above the mat: force indicator with its load cell and grip A fixed at the +y end; grip B on the motorised crosshead at the -y end, backed off 35 mm at the start (jaw faces 150 mm apart, as left after a test). Two wedge grips at the maker's drawing size: black housing 38.1 (x) x 62.2 (y) x 49.5 (z) mm, serrated jaws 19.1 mm wide, jaw gap 0-6.4 mm (horizontal jaws), thru slot open at the front and back (x), slot ends 33 mm behind the jaw faces; the slot floor's front edge has a 3 mm 45 deg lead-in. Each upper jaw is spring-closed onto the lower jaw or a tab. Its red lever handle (6 x 26 x 30 mm, top 0.135 m above the table) sits behind the housing at x 0.326 (grip A y +0.074; grip B y -0.109 at the start, moving with the crosshead); pushed 22 mm back (+x) against its return spring (6.6 N) it lifts the jaw to a 6.2 mm gap; let go, the spring returns it and the jaw spring clamps the tab with 1.9 N. Control panel at the +y end of the frame, keys up, tops 0.089 m above the mat at y 0.285: LEFT (x 0.264), STOP, RIGHT (x 0.336). While LEFT is held down the crosshead moves +y at 500 mm/min, while RIGHT is held it moves back (momentary keys), release stops it; 115.0 mm jaw-face distance is 35 mm of LEFT travel, the stop 15 mm further. Both grips start closed. Loose: one ASTM D638 Type I LDPE dogbone (165 x 19 x 3.2 mm, 13 x 57 mm neck, 7.8 g) lying flat along y on a blue specimen tray at (0.18, 0) with two 4 mm back stops at x 0.2005, underside 12 mm above the table. Behind the stand, visual only (out of reach): a PC keyboard, a mouse on its pad, a vernier caliper and safety glasses.
scoring: Scored at the last step from the end state alone; every row is a ruler, protractor or photo check. How to check by hand: a pen mark 17 mm from each tab end is hidden behind its jaw face once the tab is in that deep (photo); the slot is open at the front, so the 2 mm end gap is seen from the side and checked with a 2 mm feeler; 2 deg over the 115 mm between the jaws is a 4 mm offset (ruler or protractor). Seated = the tab is inside the slot between the jaws, past the 17 mm ruler mark at its jaw face (not beyond the slot end) and overhangs its jaw by at most 4 mm. Each grip's rows count on their own (the -y tab needs nothing from the +y tab): +0.10 +y tab seated; +0.10 lever A fully forward (within 2 mm of its forward stop: let go, the jaw spring-closed on the tab) with the +y tab seated; +0.05 the seated +y tab's end leaves a 2 mm gap to its slot end; +0.10, +0.10, +0.05 the same three rows for the -y tab and lever B. Once both tabs are seated with their levers forward: +0.15 specimen within 2 deg of the pull axis in yaw and pitch (protractor); +0.20 jaw faces 115 +- 5 mm apart (ruler; ASTM D638 distance between grips); +0.15 both grippers at least 5 cm from the specimen, both levers and both jog keys (photo). Success = full score held 3 s (the trial then ends; the hold adds no score). Possible scores 0, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.45, 0.5, 0.55, 0.6, 0.65, 0.7, 0.75, 0.8, 0.85, 0.95, 1. 0: no tab seated (not placed, on top of a jaw, off the jaw, knocked off), even with the crosshead jogged to 115 mm.
run_limit: 800 steps (40 s at 20 Hz); the demo takes about 580 steps
reset_notes: Put the dogbone back flat on its tray against the back stops, jog the crosshead back 35 mm (jaw faces 150 mm apart) and leave both levers forward. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Wedge grips at drawing size (19.1 mm jaws, 0-6.4 mm opening, thru slot), frame 460 mm (data sheet 750 mm); load cell at fixed end (maker: crosshead); props visual only. Lever: 22 mm spring-return slide lifting the spring-closed jaw to 6.2 mm. The task ends at mounting, before any pull: only the jaw spring's bite holds the tab (declared 1.9 N, no published value); the wedge self-tightens only under test load, so it is not modelled. Crosshead: position servo, 500 mm/min while a jog key is held.
